description: List the workspace's tracking domains, oldest first: the names tracked emails use for the open pixel and for links, the CNAME record to create for each, whether it is verified, and whether campaigns use it now (`inUse`). While a domain is not verified, its `dnsHost` names the DNS provider that holds its zone, read from the zone's name servers: `hosts` lists the providers they match (empty when we don't know that provider, several when more than one provider shares those names), and `dnsHost` is null when DNS did not answer in time or the domain is verified. Each campaign email uses the one under the domain it is sent from (t.acme.io for an email from ana@acme.io), or the oldest one in use when there is none. A campaign's trackOpens and trackClicks turn on once one domain is verified, but an email carries the pixel and tracked links only while a domain is `inUse`: the record is verified, our end of its target answers (`targetResolves` isn't false), and we have checked that our end serves the name over HTTPS (`httpsOkAt`). That last part is ours to set up, never yours; until it passes, emails go out without the pixel and with their links as written. `records` holds one CNAME: `name` is the full hostname, `nameInZone` is relative to `dnsHost.zone` (`@` at the zone itself, null when unknown), and `value` is its fixed target (null after an unanswered check). `check` is `verified`, `not_verified` (missing), `wrong` (see `observed`), `unanswered` or `not_checked`. `priority` is null. If `check` is `unanswered` or `not_checked`, call check_tracking_domain again before changing DNS. Write only rows with `check: not_verified` or `wrong` and a non-null `value`, using your own DNS access, then check again. At Cloudflare, keep it DNS only, not proxied. We never take a DNS password or token.
name: list_tracking_domains
title: List the tracking domains
